title: Cisco Secure Network Analytics Risk Record Volume
exclusions: Counts risk records only. It does not rank hosts, because the add-on publishes no host or score field for cisco:sna:risk.

controlTest.positiveScenario: With hosts scored in the SMC, the next input run writes cisco:sna:risk events and the latest hour is above zero.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Disable the risk collection on the input if the product exposes that choice, or stop the input. The next hour is zero.

dataSources: `index=cisco_sna sourcetype=cisco:sna:risk` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Secure Network Analytics input. Splunk's Cisco app navigator lists this sourcetype as one the add-on parses. No field list is published, so the search counts records.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Secure Network Analytics input.
spl:
index=cisco_sna sourcetype="cisco:sna:risk" earliest=-24h
| timechart span=1h count as risk_records
description: Counts Cisco Secure Network Analytics risk records per hour. The add-on writes them as cisco:sna:risk and publishes no host or score fields, so the search counts records instead of ranking hosts.
value: Risk records are how SNA points investigators at the hosts that accumulated the most suspicious traffic. If the records stop arriving, that ranking disappears from Splunk while the console still has it, and this count is how you see the gap.
implementation: Use the same Secure Network Analytics input as the alarm search, index cisco_sna. Chart cisco:sna:risk events per hour.
visualization: Column chart of risk_records per hour over 24 hours.

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide
Splunk Cisco app navigator: onboarded sourcetypes

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Risk snapshots** — if the input rewrites the whole host table each run, one hour can jump without any new risk. Treat a jump as a question for the input, not as an incident.

**Suppression:** alert on zero records during staffed hours only.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs.
• The same SMC host, domain id, username, and password as the alarm input.
• An index for this data (this page uses `cisco_sna`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the SOC.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Secure Network Analytics card, and create an input. Set the index to `cisco_sna`.
• The input writes `cisco:sna:risk`.
• Confirm events arrive: `index=cisco_sna sourcetype="cisco:sna:risk" | stats count`.

Step 2 — Create the search
```spl
index=cisco_sna sourcetype="cisco:sna:risk" earliest=-24h
| timechart span=1h count as risk_records
```

Understanding this SPL
• Same input as the alarm search. `cisco:sna:risk` is a separate sourcetype the add-on assigns to risk records.
• No score field is documented, so the panel is a volume check, not a top-hosts list.

Step 3 — Validate
• Open the host risk view in the Stealthwatch Management Console. If it lists scored hosts and this panel is zero, the risk records are not reaching the index.

• Confirm in the vendor console that the same hour shows the same kind of event before trusting a zero or a spike.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Put the panel on the SOC dashboard for Secure Network Analytics and refresh it hourly.
• Alert when the count drops to zero during a staffed period, which means the input stopped, and throttle for 4 hours.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• Alarms arrive (`cisco:sna`) but risk records do not: the input is up and the risk sourcetype is the gap. Check the input's logging settings in the user guide's SNA table.
• Neither sourcetype arrives: credentials or connectivity, same as the alarm search.
• No data for this sourcetype, with an input error in the Cisco Security Cloud log, means the credential or token is incorrect.
grandmaExplanation: We count the host risk records Cisco sends each hour, so we know that ranking of risky computers is still arriving.
